title: Test atomic TX admission and completion accounting
description:
Scope: local TX lifecycle/concurrency cases in the independent admission supplement under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/test/vectors/. Enumerate competing submissions sharing one allowance, known pre-emission driver rejection, actual emission, timeout/ambiguous completion, duplicate callbacks and stale-generation completion. Independently specify charge/release outcomes using the finalized accounting contract and actual emission evidence. Do not create an over-air reservation exchange, a delivery ACK, or a new accounting policy to hide ambiguity; unresolved contract inconsistencies must be surfaced to their owning leaf.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Test local atomic debit/settlement, not a new MAC protocol. Reuse existing scheduler and radio-event interfaces in later consumers, with event input distinct from independently expected accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Independent event ledgers prove competing admissions cannot oversubscribe a shared restriction and emitted frames are charged exactly once. A known non-emission, actual emission and ambiguous outcome follow their explicitly specified conservative treatment; duplicate/stale callbacks cannot refresh credit or imply recipient delivery. Time and generation changes preserve active restrictions. Each bounded scenario validates against the supplement schema and is consumable at the real Python/Rust/C driver boundary.
